claims.title: Beyond the Surface: Measuring Self-Preference in LLM Judgments
claims.attributed_claim: The WMT19 judging prompt compares English translations of German text; the authors limit the task scope to instruction following and translation.
claims.language_evidence: English translation targets with German source text are explicit.
claims.reviewer_boundary: Bilingual source/target material alone does not establish a matched comparison of judging responses in different languages.

claims.title: Direct Judgement Preference Optimization
claims.attributed_claim: The authors state an English evaluation focus and identify multilingual judge development as future work.
claims.reviewer_boundary: A limitation of this study is not evidence of absence across the literature.

claims.title: From Generation to Judgment: Opportunities and Challenges of LLM-as-a-judge
claims.attributed_claim: This is a survey, and it discusses existing multilingual LLM-as-a-judge research.
claims.language_evidence: Multilingual research is discussed; this excerpt is not an original experiment.
claims.reviewer_boundary: Treat surveyed findings as leads to original studies; do not count them as experiments performed by the survey.

claims.title: Arena-lite: Efficient and Reliable Large Language Model Evaluation via Tournament-Based Direct Comparisons
claims.attributed_claim: The stochastic experiment uses English-category Arena preferences; the limitations identify bracket-assignment randomness.
claims.language_evidence: English-category preferences are explicit for the cited setup.
claims.reviewer_boundary: The English-category reference applies to the stated stochastic setup. Do not extend it to every experiment without further evidence.

claims.title: Are Checklists Really Useful for Automatic Evaluation of Generative Tasks?
claims.attributed_claim: The authors identify an English-dataset limitation and report that checklists do not always improve evaluations.
claims.language_evidence: English datasets are explicit for the two stated evaluation tasks.
claims.reviewer_boundary: The checklist finding is not a measured cross-language effect.

claims.title: Analyzing Uncertainty of LLM-as-a-Judge: Interval Evaluations with Conformal Prediction
claims.attributed_claim: The paper primarily analyses summarization and reasoning, includes a GenAI-Bench appendix experiment, and notes reliance on human calibration annotations.
claims.reviewer_boundary: Do not describe the paper as exclusively text-only: the appendix records an additional experiment. Test-language coverage remains unresolved here.

claims.title: Meta-Rewarding Language Models: Self-Improving Alignment with LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge
claims.attributed_claim: The authors report persistent meta-judge positional bias as a limitation.
claims.reviewer_boundary: This is a limitation in the meta-rewarding setup, not a cross-language reliability result.

claims.title: Self-Augmented Preference Alignment for Sycophancy Reduction in LLMs
claims.attributed_claim: The evaluated sycophancy tasks are Answer Suggestion and Are You Sure; the limitations explicitly restrict the study to English.
claims.language_evidence: English-only scope is explicit in the limitations; this resolves the earlier excerpt-level Unclear for this paper.
claims.reviewer_boundary: The principal task is sycophancy assessment. Its use of an evaluator should not be conflated with a controlled multilingual judge study.

claims.title: Improve LLM-as-a-Judge Ability as a General Ability
claims.attributed_claim: The study evaluates a judge on RewardBench using official English, basic Chinese and instructional Chinese prompt variants.
claims.language_evidence: English and Chinese instruction variants are explicit; a matched response-language comparison is not established by this passage.
claims.reviewer_boundary: Instruction-language variation and response-language variation are separate dimensions. These variants also differ in instruction detail.

claims.title: Towards Optimal Evaluation Efficiency for Large Language Models
claims.attributed_claim: The experiment compares efficient subset-selection strategies and analyses reliability and semantic preservation.
claims.reviewer_boundary: Benchmark-subset reliability is a different construct from repeated LLM-judge agreement with human labels.

claims.title: CheckEval: A reliable LLM-as-a-Judge framework for evaluating text generation using checklists
claims.attributed_claim: The authors focus on summarization and dialogue response generation and identify limits of binary evaluation questions.
claims.reviewer_boundary: Do not infer language coverage from benchmark names alone. The proposed QA study below uses binary factual correctness, not a universal quality score.

claims.title: Multi-perspective Analysis of Large Language Model Domain Specialization: An Experiment in Accounting Audit Procedures Generation
claims.attributed_claim: The main instruction specifies Japanese, and Appendix B records Portuguese and Chinese evaluation prompts and an English question-answer dataset.
claims.language_evidence: Japanese, Portuguese, Chinese and English are explicitly identified in the cited settings.
claims.reviewer_boundary: The appendix changes datasets and domains. Multiple language settings alone do not establish a controlled paired language comparison.

claims.title: Debatable Intelligence: Benchmarking LLM Judges via Debate Speech Evaluation
claims.attributed_claim: The experiments run multiple LLM judges on debate speeches and measure agreement with humans.
claims.reviewer_boundary: This supports a human-agreement study in debate evaluation; multilingual coverage is not established by this passage.

claims.title: Beyond the Score: Uncertainty-Calibrated LLMs for Automated Essay Assessment
claims.attributed_claim: The authors explicitly restrict the study to English and three public essay corpora.
claims.reviewer_boundary: This is an essay-scoring scope limitation, not evidence that multilingual judging is unstudied elsewhere.

claims.title: MR. Judge: Multimodal Reasoner as a Judge
claims.attributed_claim: MR. Judge formulates judgment as a reasoning-inspired multiple-choice problem and notes an evaluation-time cost.
claims.reviewer_boundary: Multimodal content and multilingual evaluation are different dimensions.

claims.title: Co-Eval: Augmenting LLM-based Evaluation with Machine Metrics
claims.attributed_claim: The translation experiment explicitly uses six target languages and the limitations mention metric-selection mismatches.
claims.language_evidence: Six target languages are explicit; resource-level classification is not established here.
claims.reviewer_boundary: This is evidence that multilingual evaluation exists in the corpus. The quoted setup does not justify assigning universal language-resource categories.

claims.title: Model Consistency as a Cheap yet Predictive Proxy for LLM Elo Scores
claims.attributed_claim: The authors state that the dataset human preference annotations were not used and identify difficulty distinguishing top-performing models.
claims.reviewer_boundary: Separate unused item-level human labels from the paper's comparison with Arena Elo scores; do not label the work as having no human-derived reference of any kind.

claims.title: Can Large Language Models Outperform Non-Experts in Poetry Evaluation? A Comparative Study Using the Consensual Assessment Technique
claims.attributed_claim: The study uses 90 English-language poems, includes repeated evaluations, and calls for direct expert validation.
claims.reviewer_boundary: Repeated-run reliability, performance against non-experts and validation by expert raters are distinct claims.
